message:
I have this dear friend, Linda, who is always the first to panic at the slightest hint of trouble. Just the other day, she called me in a frenzy because a storm was rolling in, and she was convinced we’d be cut off from the world. While I appreciated her concern, I couldn’t help but chuckle a little—my go-bag was all packed, and I had enough water stored to last through a week of storms. 

I gently reminded her that being prepared doesn’t mean living in fear; it’s about finding peace in knowing we’re ready for whatever comes our way. We laughed about it, but it also made me think: maybe I could help her feel a bit more at ease by sharing some of my own tips on readiness. Have you ever had to reassure a friend who tends to jump to the worst-case scenario?
